title: Phase 6 - Statistical validation: woo_benchmark and solver pins through the fast core
description: Rerun the documented accuracy chain on the fast engine: solver pins (within 10 bp, sub-bp at 2+ decks), fresh-shoe agreement bands (about +6 bp at 1-2 decks and +1.5 bp at 6 decks vs solver best_ev), and a large-sample cardsharp/tools/woo_benchmark.py run (40M games per config). Update the Accuracy Validation Chain section of docs/optimization_principles.md with fast-core results and date. Record single-core throughput alongside, before in-core parallelism lands, so the speedup attribution stays clean.
close_reason: 1B-round fast-core validation complete: sim-WoO/sim-solver in documented bands at all 5 pinned configs, continuation-gap interpretation documented, accuracy chain updated, throughput recorded pre-Rayon (1.2-2.3M games/s single core).

title: Phase 5 - Card-stream parity suite: Rust core vs Python reference engine
description: The accuracy gate. Python generates shuffled shoe orders (including adversarial hand-built and property-based sequences); both engines play the identical card stream; assert per-round equality of decisions, payouts, bankroll deltas, and cards consumed. Must cover splits and resplits, split aces, surrender fallbacks (Rh/Rs), insurance, dealer blackjack peek and no-peek, cut-card timing across rounds, and mid-round shoe exhaustion. Wire into CI as a required check. This implements the testing-optimization-correctness procedure in docs/optimization_principles.md: same inputs, identical outcomes, edge cases thoroughly.
notes: Suite: tests/test_fastsim_parity.py (30 tests, ~5s). Money flow, per-hand outcomes, and cards consumed compared exactly across 19 weighted fuzz configs and crafted adversarial streams; shuffle timing compared via consumption-count epochs (cardsharp_core.trace_shoe + counters on both shoes), which is RNG-independent and therefore exact. Known coverage limit: per-decision action sequences are asserted on Rust records for crafted cases but only proxied (via money/consumption equality) for fuzz cases, since play_game does not expose action_history; over thousands of fuzzed rounds any decision divergence necessarily perturbs money or consumption. Full suite run 2026-06-09: 775 passed; one solver test exceeds 300s solo (6m42s) so any future pytest-timeout config needs a higher ceiling.
close_reason: Parity suite complete: 30 tests, 19 fuzz configs + adversarial streams + RNG-free shuffle-timing traces covering cut card and mid-round exhaustion. All pass first run; wired into fast-core CI job.

title: Phase 2 - Scaffold crates/cardsharp-core: PyO3 + maturin wired into uv and CI
description: Create the Rust workspace at crates/cardsharp-core with PyO3 bindings and maturin as the build backend, buildable via uv so the extension imports as cardsharp_core. Add a CI job that builds the crate and runs a smoke test (import plus one trivial round-trip call). Decide packaging posture: optional accelerator (extras tag or build-from-source) with the pure-Python path remaining the default fallback. Deliverable: an empty-but-building extension exposing one function.
close_reason: Scaffold complete: crate builds via uv sync --extra fast, smoke tests pass, fmt+clippy clean, CI fast-core job added

title: Phase 3 - Rust round engine: shoe, hands, basic strategy, full action set (flat path)
description: Implement the complete single-round engine in idiomatic Rust: int-encoded cards; Shoe with penetration and cut-card semantics matching the Python Shoe.begin_round/end_round contract (the cut card never interrupts a round; mid-round exhaustion reshuffles only the discards); hand struct with incremental totals; splits and resplits, split aces, doubles, surrender with the Rh/Rs fallback, insurance, dealer H17/S17, payouts including blackjack bonus; dealer draws only while a live player hand exists. Strategy arrives from Python as a compiled lookup array built from the existing CSV charts or solver output. Two entry points: simulate_batch(rules, table, n_rounds, seed) returning aggregates, and play_card_stream(cards, rules, table) for parity injection. Style requirement: enums and exhaustive match, no magic ints in game logic - the compiler enforces rule coverage.
notes: Engine complete, validated 2026-06-09. Throughput: 2,649,089 rounds/s single-threaded (20M-round run) vs 51,154/s for the Python engine at identical rules = 51x, before any tuning or parallelism. Parity evidence: 21,360 random card-stream rounds across 2,000 streams with ZERO mismatches vs the Python engine on net/total/initial bets, per-hand winners, and cards consumed; committed fuzz covers peek, no-peek, no-peek+insurance, and S17+resplit configs (tests/test_fastsim_core.py). Statistical sanity: 50M-round fresh-shoe HE at 6d H17 DAS LS = 0.6528 +/- 0.031 pct, consistent with published basic-strategy values and the documented solver chain; Python engine cross-checks agree within ~1.5 sigma at its attainable power (tight gate is beads-9ro.6). Quirks of the reference engine deliberately preserved and documented in round.rs: HIT on any split hand containing an ace is refused (forced stand) even when hit_split_aces would allow it; resplit_aces unreachable via the state path; surrendered hands get phantom win/loss tallies from the hand-value comparison. Rank-only cards (suits provably dead for classic variant: ClassicPayoutCalculator bypasses the bonus-combination branch). simulate_batch returns a SimulationStats.report()-shaped dict consumed directly by from_dict; play_card_stream returns full per-round records for the Phase 5 suite.
close_reason: Engine complete: 51x throughput, zero-mismatch stream parity vs reference engine, fresh-shoe HE consistent with accuracy chain. Full suite green (737 passed).

title: Phase 1 - Profile baseline: py-spy flame graph of single-CPU simulation hot path
description: Before building anything, capture where the ~45 microseconds per round actually goes. Run py-spy record (flamegraph output) against a --simulate --single_cpu run. Confirm or refute the code-reading hypothesis: per-round Player/BlackjackGame construction in play_game (blackjack.py:519), per-round stats dict round-trip (report / from_dict / merge in play_game_batch), unconditional f-string construction in state handlers and decision_logger call sites (state.py:338, state.py:433), and the dict-based hand value cache (hand.py:22). Deliverable: flame graph artifact plus ranked notes on this issue. This is the before picture every later phase is measured against.
notes: Baseline captured 2026-06-09 on Apple Silicon / CPython 3.14.3: 51,843 games/s native single-CPU (19.3 us/round) at seed 12345 - the 22k figure in docs is stale for this hardware. Artifacts: docs/perf/flame-single-cpu-2026-06-09.speedscope.json + .html (pyinstrument; py-spy needs root on macOS, sudo command documented in docs/perf/baseline-single-cpu-2026-06-09.md). All four churn hypotheses CONFIRMED: per-round Game/Player/Dealer construction ~12 pct; stats report/from_dict/merge round-trip ~7 pct; unconditional f-strings + no-op game.output (463k calls per 50k rounds) inside the ~18 pct state-handler self-time; dict-based hand cache costs 1M dict.get per 50k rounds (value() called 12.6x per round). Strategy lookup ~4 pct and shoe ~2 pct - both already cheap. Bonus finding: state.py:269 blackjack announcement is outside its if-block, formatting for every player every round (display bug, invisible in sim mode). Conclusion: overhead is smeared across CPython object machinery, no single hotspot; micro-opts cap ~1.5-2x; validates the Rust-core plan in beads-9ro.3.
close_reason: Deliverables complete: flame graph artifacts in docs/perf/, ranked notes on issue, baseline doc committed

title: Rust fast-core blackjack simulation engine behind a readable Python facade
description:
Goal: dramatic simulation throughput (target: millions of rounds/sec single core, tens of millions parallel, vs ~22k single-thread / ~350k multiprocess today) without sacrificing readability or the accuracy chain.

Decision (2026-06-09): implement the hot loop as a Rust crate (crates/cardsharp-core) exposed via PyO3/maturin, behind a thin Python facade (cardsharp/fastsim). Rust chosen over Numba/Cython because zero-cost abstractions keep the fast code itself readable - enums, structs, and exhaustive match read like the rulebook - while fast-Python dialects degrade into int-coded soup. The existing event-driven Python engine stays as the executable reference implementation and interactive engine; the Rust core is an optional accelerator with graceful fallback, so contributors without Rust keep a fully working system.

Accuracy strategy per docs/optimization_principles.md: (1) card-stream injection parity - both engines play identical injected card sequences, asserting identical decisions, payouts, and shoe positions (avoids coupling the RNGs); (2) the existing statistical anchors - solver pins, WoO benchmark bands, fresh-shoe convergence - rerun through the fast core. Strategy charts stay CSV + Python solver as the source of truth; Rust consumes compiled lookup tables.

Phases: profile baseline; scaffold crate/build; core round engine; Python facade + fallback; card-stream parity suite; statistical validation; in-core parallelism (Rayon); feature extensions (counting, CSM, shuffles); variance reduction (conditional dealer settlement, CRN). Variance reduction compounds multiplicatively with engine speed.

title: Simulator accuracy: fix mid-round shoe reshuffle, dead-hand dealer draws, add exact convergence target
description: The Monte Carlo simulator has systematic fidelity gaps vs both real casino procedure and the solver's modeled game: (1) Shoe.deal() reshuffles the moment the cut card index is crossed, even mid-round, and the shuffle re-includes cards currently held by players/dealer, so a round can contain duplicate copies of a physical card (worst at 1 deck where 1-in-7 rounds straddles the cut card); real games finish the round, then shuffle. (2) DealersTurnState always plays out the dealer hand even when every player hand is busted/surrendered/settled; real dealers do not draw, which distorts shoe pacing and lets counting strategies see cards a real counter never would. (3) The solver's house_edge assumes composition-dependent 2-card play, while the simulator plays the collapsed total-based table, so there is no exact target to validate the simulator against -- tests use a 4-sigma/1% tolerance that hides 10-30bp biases. Fix the shoe with round-aware dealing (begin/end round hooks, cut-card honored between rounds, exhaustion reshuffle excludes in-play cards), gate dealer draws on a live hand existing, add a table-EV (total-dependent) house edge to the solver as the simulator's exact convergence target, then pin simulator-vs-solver with tight CIs in fresh-shoe mode.
notes: Fixed: (1) Shoe round-aware dealing (begin_round/end_round; cut card defers shuffle to between rounds; mid-round exhaustion reshuffles discards only, in-play cards excluded; legacy path preserved for baccarat/dragon-tiger). (2) Dealer completes hand only when a live player hand remains. (3) strategy_house_edge() added: exact EV of the collapsed TD table = simulator's convergence target. (4) SolverStrategy(use_ev_table=True) / --cd_strategy plays composition-dependent first decisions = converges to house_edge itself. (5) Strategy-table generation bug: hard 17 was hardcoded Stand; now surrenders vs A under H17 (worth 0.42bp at 6d); CSV + S17 patch + Rh/Rs fallback updated. Measured: 1d 0.75pen gap +30bp -> +20bp (cut-card effect is real and stays); 6d fresh-shoe CD converges within -2.2bp +/- 4.5bp. OUTSTANDING: 1d fresh-shoe CD residual +9.7bp +/- 4.5 vs solver; per-deal-category diagnostic running; hypothesis: solver draws player cards from unconditioned deck-minus-3 in peek games (standard CA approximation) while the sim is physically correct; note WoO sits +7.3bp above solver at 1d H17 which matches the sim residual within noise.
close_reason: All three simulator accuracy defects fixed and validated: (1) round-aware shoe (no mid-round cut-card shuffle, no in-play duplicate deals), (2) dealer draws only with live hands, (3) exact convergence targets (strategy_house_edge + --cd_strategy) plus the hard-17-vs-A surrender table bug found along the way. Measured: 1d 0.75-pen bias +30bp -> +20bp (remainder is the genuine cut-card effect vs the solver's fresh-shoe model); 6d fresh-shoe converges to the solver within -2.2 +/- 4.5bp; 1d fresh-shoe residual +7bp fully attributed to the solver's full-CD continuation optimum (sim matches WoO within ~1bp), resolving the prior WoO-gap investigation. Suites green: 712 non-slow + 14 slow. Follow-up: beads-u0h.

comments.author: Matt Michie
comments.text: CORRECTION (2026-06-09, found by beads-caz benchmark): the close reason's claim 'sim matches WoO within ~1bp' was wrong -- it relied on the prior session's 1d-H17 gap figures ('-7.3/-7.95 bp') which carried a 10x units slip; the true solver-vs-WoO gaps are -0.73/-0.80 bp. Direct 40M-game-per-config measurement shows: solver matches WoO within ~1bp at ALL five configs (including 1 deck), and the SIMULATOR sits above both by +5 to +6.3bp at 1-2 decks (the table-expressiveness/continuation-CD residual, decomposition-confirmed) and by ~+3bp +/- 3.1 at 6 decks (precision run pending). The mechanics fixes and convergence infrastructure in this issue are unaffected.

title: Rules-surface tripwire: new Rules fields must be mapped or refused
description: The only silent drift path between engines: a new field added to Python Rules is honored by the reference engine but silently dropped by fastsim.rules_kwargs, so the core plays old rules while resolve_engine reports the config as supported. Add a test asserting every key of Rules().to_dict() (plus constructor-only fields like allow_obo) is either explicitly mapped by rules_kwargs or explicitly listed in an UNSUPPORTED set that makes resolve_engine fall back with a reason. A new field then fails CI with instructions instead of producing silent wrong answers. Bridge work for the dual-engine period; obsoleted by beads-i2s.6.
close_reason: Tripwire test landed: 22 mapped, 2 refused, 3 inert-with-parity-coverage fields; new fields fail CI with classification instructions.

title: Estimator paths run without the Python engine: CV and friends
description: The --cv control variate currently requires the Python engine (per-round deal-state capture feeding the deal-EV table Y). Before retirement, either compute the deal-Y inside the core (it knows the deal; Python supplies the EV table, the core returns CV accumulators in the report dict) or supersede the deal-EV CV with beads-9ro.9's conditional dealer settlement where that lands. Acceptance: every CLI estimator flag works with the Python round engine deleted, or is explicitly retired with a documented replacement.

title: Port the per-deal EV diagnostic to the fast core
description: cardsharp/tools/deal_ev_diagnostic.py decomposes simulator-vs-solver gaps per deal (it attributed the 1-deck WoO residual entirely to play EV). It currently drives the Python engine. Add a fast-core leg so this forensic capability survives the Python engine's retirement: per-deal aggregation needs the core to bucket round outcomes by (card1, card2, upcard), either via a dedicated entry point or an optional per-deal accumulator in simulate_batch. This tool is the standing instrument for investigating any future divergence from the solver.

title: Interactive session API on the fast core
description: Inversion-of-control round API so the core can drive interactive play: either a resumable session object (session.step() returns dealt cards/events so far plus the pending decision context -- seat, hand, valid actions; session.apply(action) continues) or a decision callback passed to play_round_interactive. GIL round-trips per decision are irrelevant at human speeds. Step records must carry every fact the event emitter needs so the existing event-driven architecture can layer on top unchanged. Custom user-written Python strategies ride the same path (at roughly old-engine speeds, acceptable). Design note: prefer the resumable session over callbacks if pyo3 reentrancy gets awkward.

title: Migrate console and web adapters to the core session API
description: The CLI console mode and web adapter currently drive the Python round engine directly. Rewire them onto the core session API: the event emitter becomes a translation layer from step records to events; player input feeds session.apply. Behavior parity with the old interactive flow verified by transcript comparison on scripted inputs. After this lands, no production path constructs the Python round engine for play.

title: Golden card-stream regression corpus
description: Freeze parity-proven behavior as data: generate a corpus of card streams across every supported rule configuration (including Phase 8 features once ported), record play_card_stream outputs (hands, actions, winners, money flow, cards consumed), and commit them. A test replays the corpus through the core and asserts exact equality. This regression-locks the engine against its own verified history without needing a second engine alive. Document the update procedure: intentional semantic changes regenerate goldens in a reviewable diff, never silently.

title: Single-engine end state: Rust core canonical, Python engine retired
description:
Decision (2026-06-10): the dual-engine architecture (Python reference + Rust fast core kept equivalent by the parity suite) is scaffolding, not the end state. Long term, exactly one implementation of the game rules survives -- the Rust core -- and Python becomes the API/orchestration layer above it (stats, CIs, solver, strategy charts, adapters, UI, CLI).

Rationale. Python-canonical is unworkable: there is no mechanical path from idiomatic Python to fast Rust, so the core would forever be hand-synced, which is the drift problem made permanent. A shared declarative spec is a trap: charts and rule config are already shared data; what is duplicated is imperative round flow, and a spec rich enough to express it is a third implementation. Rust-canonical works once the core gains an interactive session API (inversion of control: decision callback or resumable session; the event-driven architecture survives as a translation layer over step records).

Verification after retirement does NOT regress: the combinatorial solver is the genuinely independent second implementation (exact enumeration vs Monte Carlo, pinned to WoO within ~1 bp) and is a stronger independence property than two simulators sharing a design. Add golden card-stream regression data (frozen parity-proven outputs) for drift-locking, and port the per-deal diagnostic so future gaps decompose against the solver. Honest residual: path-dependent quantities (cut-card, counting EV) have no exact oracle in any architecture; published numbers + goldens + review cover them, as they always did.

Costs accepted: Python-only contributors cannot edit game rules; rules experiments need a ~6s crate rebuild. Gates: do not start until beads-9ro.8 (feature-complete core) and beads-9ro.9 (estimator paths) land; the parity suite remains load-bearing during construction and is deleted only at the end.

Sequence: session API -> adapter migration; golden corpus; diagnostic port; CV/estimators without the Python engine; then freeze -> one-release deprecation -> delete engine + parity suite + fallback paths.

title: Flaky test: test_full_game_cycle assumes a player decision always happens
description: tests/integration/test_blackjack_integration.py::test_full_game_cycle asserts PLAYER_DECISION_NEEDED is among the emitted events, but a natural blackjack on the initial deal legitimately ends the hand before any decision is needed, so the test fails intermittently (measured 1 failure in 10 runs on 2026-06-09, CPython 3.14.3). Fails in isolation on an unmodified tree - not caused by any recent change; surfaced during full-suite verification for beads-9ro.2. Fix options: seed or force the dealt cards so a decision phase is guaranteed, or make the assertion conditional on the dealt hands not being naturals.

title: Phase 7 - In-core parallelism: Rayon batches, GIL release, slim worker IPC
description: Parallelize batches inside the crate with per-shard seeded RNG streams, reproducible by construction: for a given master seed, shard results are identical regardless of thread count (per-shard PRNG instances, deterministic merge). Release the GIL during simulate. On the Python side, stop shipping the per-round earnings list back from workers unless --vis is set (it is a large pickle on big runs), and retire the multiprocessing path for fast-core runs. Target near-linear scaling to physical cores; record the new throughput numbers.
notes: Implemented 2026-06-10. Design: fixed 250k-round shards, per-shard seeds derived via explicit SplitMix64 from the master seed, each shard runs a self-contained fresh shoe, rayon par_iter map preserves shard order, sequential Chan/Welford fold (SimStats::merge mirrors stats.py merge op-for-op). Result: bit-identical aggregates for a given seed at ANY thread count (test_simulate_batch_results_are_thread_count_invariant: 1 == 2 == all-cores at 600k rounds). GIL released via Python::detach for the whole simulation. Measured on 14 logical cores (Apple Silicon): 2.87M rounds/s at threads=1, 29.75M rounds/s all cores = 10.4x scaling (near-linear to the ~10 performance cores); CLI end-to-end 29.7M games/s, 100M games in 3.4s. Cumulative: 574x the Python single-thread baseline, 85x the old multiprocess default. The fresh-shoe boundary every 250k rounds matches what multiprocess Python workers already did. IPC fix: play_game_batch ships the per-round earnings list only when collect_earnings is set (only --vis consumes it); woo_benchmark gains --threads. At 100M games the CLI default S17 config reads HE 0.4735 +/- 0.022 pct, matching published 6d S17 DAS LS + cut-card expectations.
close_reason: 29.75M rounds/s all-core (10.4x scaling), bit-identical results across thread counts with regression test, GIL released, IPC slimmed. Suite green (777 passed).

title: Phase 4 - Python facade cardsharp/fastsim with graceful fallback to the reference engine
description: Thin readable wrapper: map the Rules object to the core config, map core aggregates into SimulationStats, and expose the same run surface the CLI uses. If the extension is missing, fall back to the existing Python engine transparently (identical results guaranteed by the parity suite). Add CLI selection: default to the fast core when available, with a flag to force the reference engine. Orchestration, stats, confidence intervals, control variates, and plotting stay in Python - the readable layer.
close_reason: Facade complete: simulate()/resolve_engine()/run_fast_batch(), CLI --engine flag with honest reporting, 2.7M games/s through the CLI, all fallback paths smoke-tested, docs refreshed. Suite green (775 passed).

title: WoO benchmark runner: big sim vs Wizard of Odds reference values
description: Add cardsharp/tools/woo_benchmark.py: for each of the 5 WoO-calculator-pinned rule sets (1d/2d/6d, H17/S17; no-DAS, LS, peek, no-resplit, 3:2), run a large multiprocess fresh-shoe simulation with the composition-dependent solver strategy and CV, and report simulator HE vs WoO Optimal vs our solver with confidence intervals. This empirically tests the beads-8o8 conclusion that the simulator reproduces WoO's optimal numbers (table-achievable play) at 1 deck where our solver computes a stronger full-CD optimum.
close_reason: Benchmark shipped (cardsharp/tools/woo_benchmark.py) and run: 360M games total (40M per config across the 5 WoO-pinned rule sets + 160M 6dH17 precision run). Results: solver matches WoO Optimal within ~1bp at every config (the prior '7bp 1d gap' was a 10x units slip, now corrected in TestWoOReference and docs); simulator sits above both by the table-vs-full-CD achievability gap, ~+6bp at 1-2 decks shrinking to ~+1.5bp at 6 decks, decomposition-attributed entirely to play EV with zero deal-mix bias.

description: Run the parity suite under pytest --cov scoped to cardsharp/blackjack/state.py, actor.py, and strategy.py and enumerate unexercised branches in the round flow; add fuzz configs or crafted streams until the reachable branches are covered, so the suite's sensitivity is known rather than assumed. title: Nightly randomized parity fuzz workflow
description: The CI parity fuzz uses fixed seeds: reproducible but frozen coverage. Add a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (cron, off the PR path) that runs the same stream-parity harness for a few minutes with a fresh random master seed, printing the seed and failing codes on divergence for exact reproduction. Keeps probing new card sequences for the life of the dual-engine period. Bridge work; obsoleted by beads-i2s.6 (goldens replace it).

title: Freeze, deprecate, then delete the Python round engine and parity suite
description: The retirement itself, in stages: (1) freeze the Python round engine -- no new features, parity suite still green; (2) one release with --engine python marked deprecated and a runtime warning; (3) delete the engine (state machine, actor round logic, engine-side Shoe paths), the parity suite, and the fallback branches; resolve_engine collapses; docs and the Accuracy Validation Chain are rewritten around solver + goldens + WoO pins as the verification stack. The golden corpus and the diagnostic port must be merged and stable for at least one release before step 3. Net effect: one rules implementation, drift structurally impossible.

title: strategy_house_edge docstring understates the TD-continuation residual
description: The caveat in cardsharp/blackjack/solver/engine.py strategy_house_edge says the residual from composition-sensitive post-hit boundaries is an order of magnitude smaller than the first-decision effect. The 2026-06-09 fast-core measurement (woo_benchmark --engine fast, 200M games/config, +/-1.6 bp) shows the opposite ordering at every pinned config: continuation residual +6.3/+7.6 bp at 1 deck vs first-decision effect +2.7/+4.9 bp; at 6 decks +2.9/+4.1 bp vs ~0.02 bp. The structural account in the accuracy chain is confirmed; only the magnitude claim is wrong. Fix the docstring, and optionally extend deal_ev_diagnostic to decompose the continuation residual per deal the way the 1-deck WoO gap investigation did.

title: Install pytest-timeout with a suite-appropriate ceiling (600s)
description: The per-module pytest.ini files reference a timeout option but the pytest-timeout plugin is not installed, so it is silently ignored (pytest warns Unknown config option: timeout). On 2026-06-09 a full-suite run deadlocked indefinitely (xdist workers at 0 pct CPU, orphaned multiprocessing resource_tracker processes, likely a macOS fork flake under parallel load) and only manual inspection caught it. Add pytest-timeout to dev dependencies and set a ceiling around 600s with thread method: the slowest legitimate test (tests/blackjack/solver/test_engine.py TestAutoMode::test_auto_three_deck_routes_to_exact) takes 6m42s solo, so a 300s ceiling kills it (observed: reported as a worker crash, since the thread method terminates the worker process). Consider also marking that solver test as slow and excluding it from default runs.
notes: Follow-up commit required: pytest config discovery uses the ini NEAREST the path arguments, so the ceiling had to land in all six pytest.ini files (root for no-arg runs, tests/ for path-arg runs incl. the CI fast-core job, and the four per-directory inis). Also defused tests/integration/pytest.ini timeout=5, which predated the plugin and became armed (and dangerous) the moment the dependency was installed. Enforcement proven by probe in both invocation styles. Lesson recorded: this repo has six pytest.ini files with different governance per invocation style; the root pyproject [tool.pytest.ini_options] is fully shadowed.
close_reason: pytest-timeout 2.4 added as dev dep; 1800s thread-method ceiling in the root pytest.ini (600s would kill the 7-min-local solver test on slower CI runners). Verified header engagement.

title: Phase 9 - Variance reduction: conditional dealer settlement and CRN for rule comparisons
description: Two estimator upgrades that compound multiplicatively with engine speed. (1) Conditional dealer settlement (Rao-Blackwellization): once player hands are fixed, record the exact expected payoff over the dealer outcome distribution computed from the remaining shoe composition (machinery exists in cardsharp/blackjack/solver/dealer.py; port to the core, memoized by composition signature) while still physically drawing dealer cards so the shoe trajectory and cut-card dynamics are unchanged. Unbiased by the tower property; validate empirically that the mean matches the plain estimator and measure the variance reduction. (2) Common random numbers for run_rule_comparison: identical master seeds and shoe sequences across rule variants so EV differences get dramatically tighter confidence intervals. Document measured effective speedups (time to a target CI width).
notes: Both estimator upgrades implemented and measured 2026-06-10. (1) Conditional dealer settlement (settle.rs): hole-known Rao-Blackwellization -- exact dealer-outcome distribution by without-replacement recursion over the remaining shoe composition (ten-classes collapsed, exactness preserved), dealer still draws physically. Scope: peek + non-CSM only (no-peek dealer BJ reroutes payouts through OBO/void; documented). Upcard-only averaging (the solver's view, bigger reduction) deliberately not attempted: exact per-composition dealer distributions cost more than the simulation itself. Validated: same-seed runs play identical physical rounds and means agree (sharp unbiasedness test); hand-computed conditional values exact on crafted streams; found and fixed an ace-counts-11-on-high-totals bug in the dealer state machine via the unbiasedness test (+3 pct player bias, now regression-tested). MEASURED: 1.83x variance reduction at 2.75x (fresh-shoe) to 4.3x (pen 0.75) throughput cost = net 0.42-0.67x time-to-CI -- a NET LOSS on this engine (35ns rounds are too cheap for a ~150ns settlement to beat at 1.83x). Feature ships validated and OFF by default; honest finding documented in the accuracy chain. (2) CRN paired comparison (simulate_paired + compare_rules engine=auto fast path, mirroring comparison.py semantics: per-round common decks, paired Welford, thread-count-invariant Chan merges): H17-S17 at 2M rounds = +19.05bp +/- 2.30bp, 9.6x tighter CI than independent runs (~92x effective rounds), seconds vs the Python CRN path's ~90 minutes. Identical-variant diff is exactly zero (regression test). CLI --compare_rules now auto-selects the core.

title: Phase 8 - Extend fast core: counting strategies, CSM, realistic shuffles, variants
description: Port the remaining simulation features to the fast core: hi-lo counting with true-count bet ramp and play deviations, CSM mode, GSR riffle and strip shuffle models with configurable shuffle counts, burn cards, and deck variants (deck_factory equivalents). Each feature lands only with extended parity coverage plus a statistical cross-check against the Python engine; counting behavior also validated against the existing counting tests (count reset on reshuffle, decks-remaining tracking).
notes: Slice 1/3 (counting) complete 2026-06-10. Hi-Lo in the core (counting.rs) mirrors CountingStrategy exactly: pending-card queue folded into the count only at play decisions (so bets and insurance use the round-start count while decisions see all dealt cards including the dealer hole card -- reference quirk preserved); Illustrious 18 deviations cross as DATA from strategy._COUNTING_DEVIATIONS so Python stays the source of truth; bet ramp 1/4/8/12/20x with toward-zero TC truncation; insurance at TC>=3; reshuffle detection via cards-remaining increase with post-reset round recount; decks_remaining = max(0.5, remaining/52). Counter is per-shard, preserving thread-count invariance (regression-tested). Validation: 6 counting parity fuzz configs (950 multi-round streams incl. high-TC, negative-TC, S17, no-peek, resplit), crafted ramp test, statistical band -- all green first run; 70/70 fastsim tests. CLI --strat count now runs the fast core: 24.7M games/s, measured player edge +1.07 pct +/- 0.13 at 10M games (6d S17 DAS LS 75 pct pen, 1-20 spread) -- textbook Hi-Lo. Known doc'd divergence: id-dedup after mid-round exhaustion (unreachable below pen ~1.0). Remaining slices: CSM mode, GSR riffle/strip shuffles. Scope note: non-classic variants (Spanish 21) stay on the reference engine -- they need validators/payouts beyond deck composition and resolve_engine already refuses them; revisit only when a concrete variant matters.
close_reason: All three slices landed: Hi-Lo counting (parity-exact, 950 fuzz streams), CSM, GSR riffle + strip shuffles (mechanical invariants + statistical bands). Variants scope-noted out. CLI: counting 24.7M/s, CSM 21.5M/s, riffle 14.5M/s.

title: Optional full-CD continuation play mode for the simulator
description: The solver's best_ev embeds composition-dependent stand-vs-hit re-optimization at every post-hit card (player._ev_hit recurses with the depleted deck). The simulator -- even with --cd_strategy, which plays the first decision per (card1,card2,upcard) -- uses the total-based table for 3+ card hands, leaving an achievability gap measured at ~+6bp at 1-2 decks and ~+1.5bp at 6 decks (woo_benchmark 40M/config + 160M 6d precision run, 2026-06-09; 12M-round decomposition attributes it entirely to play EV, zero deal-mix bias). Note our solver and the WoO calculator agree within ~1bp at every pinned config -- both are full-CD optima. If we ever want the simulator to achieve that optimum (e.g. to validate the solver's continuation model empirically), add a play mode that queries ev_hit/ev_stand on the live hand composition during PlayersTurn. Expensive per decision; likely needs memoization per (hand-state, deck-key) and is only worth it for 1-2 deck research runs. Also consider the converse: a solver mode whose hit recursion is restricted to table-expressible continuations, giving an exact target for table players at any deck count.

value: Architecture decision 2026-06-10: the Rust core (crates/cardsharp-core) becomes the canonical rules engine long-term; the Python round engine retires after epics beads-9ro phases 8-9 complete. Tracked as epic beads-i2s with full rationale in its description. Key points: parity suite is scaffolding deleted at the end; the combinatorial solver (not the Python engine) is the genuinely independent verifier; golden card-stream data replaces live parity; interactive play moves to a core session API with the event system as a translation layer. Until then the dual-engine discipline holds: round-semantics changes land in both engines with parity proven (CLAUDE.md), plus bridge tasks beads-366 (rules tripwire), beads-7fz (nightly fuzz), beads-l59 (coverage audit).
